I’m 49 this year, and I’ve worked these fields for 30 years, so I don’t like making big changes unless there is a clear reason. With only 7.5 mu and two people in the house, I have to keep things steady and not spend too aggressively at the start. I’ll still keep the wheat-maize rotation on most of the land because that is the safest income for me, and I’ll leave a smaller piece in cotton because cotton spreads the risk and gives me another cash crop. I finished last year seeing that wheat and maize still pay more steadily if I manage water in time, but cotton can help if grain prices are weak, so this year I’ll do about 5 mu in wheat-maize and 2.5 mu in cotton. For wheat, I’ll follow the usual local timing, use a common improved variety, put most of the fertilizer down as base plus one topdress at jointing, and irrigate around wintering, jointing, and filling if the weather is dry. For summer maize, the key is speed after wheat harvest, so I won’t waste time with heavy tillage, just quick residue handling and sowing. Cotton I’ll keep a bit lighter on fertilizer than grain land because I need to watch cash, but I’ll still irrigate at the important stages if the well cost is manageable.

I don’t count everything like a scientist, but I do look at what happened before. Last year when the wheat got water on time, the yield was decent, so I won’t save money by skipping irrigation if the crop needs it. Fertilizer also can’t be cut too much, because if wheat or maize turns pale later, the lost yield hurts more than the saved few yuan. Still, I won’t chase the highest possible yield. I need a plan I can afford and finish with only two people.
